clue.text: In front of kilns see black crows

indicators.note: the piece for black is placed ahead of the piece for kilns

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
oasts are kilns for drying hops

explanation.surface: Black crows perched in front of the hop kilns, seen across the Kent countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like the birds but is the verb. Oast houses are the round hop kilns of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag loudly, so crows is a synonym of the verb form here.

clue.text: Give in, having suffered relegation again?

definitions.meaning: to concede or retreat from a position
dropped to a lower division once more, as a sports team might be

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the phrasal verb for yielding; the other reads it literally as being sent down a second time.

clue.text: The interminable love record in any collection

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed within the word any
having no end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An endless love song shows up in any compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' cuts the last letter of The, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered set of poems or stories by various writers is a literary collection.

clue.text: Men who strike yet order daily paper

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Striking workers still order their daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous American newspaper published every day in Manhattan.

clue.text: Traitor who, in France, faces the rope

indicators.note: one piece stands facing, that is ahead of, the other in the answer

parts.note: qui is French for who
a sling is a rope or strap used for hoisting or carrying

explanation.surface: A French traitor is led out to meet the hangman's noose.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling collaborated with the Nazis, and his name became a byword for a collaborator or betrayer.

clue.text: Apply anti-rust treatment to submarine near loch

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits right next to the word for submarine

parts.note: submarine as an adjective means beneath the sea
L is a map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Rustproofing a submarine moored near a Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: To coat a vehicle's underside with a protective layer against corrosion is this verb.

clue.text: Revolving components on various cheap Fords nearly broke

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits on top of the other
turning round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: parts are components

indicators.note: the letters appear in a different, varied arrangement

explanation.surface: A mechanic fitting parts to old cheap Fords is almost bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolving' turns PARTS into STRAP; 'various' rearranges CHEAP FORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money means nearly out of funds, an idiom for being almost penniless.

clue.text: Bloody liquid concoction in cans — hope one's refreshing when opened

indicators.note: opening each word reveals only its first letter

explanation.surface: A blood-red energy drink in a can, hoped to be refreshing once you open it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in the veins of the gods in place of blood.

clue.text: It could be found in Gironde, vacant

definitions.text: It could be found in Gironde, vacant

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the other letters
emptied of its inside, leaving just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A vacant holiday home might be found in the Gironde region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' leaves GE from Gironde; It goes inside. The whole clue also defines: a French holiday cottage might be found empty in Gironde.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural French holiday cottage for rent, of the kind found in Gironde in south-west France.

clue.text: A holiday is over: here's souvenir from Spain, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means read from bottom to top

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday

explanation.surface: The holiday has ended, and here is a keepsake brought back from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish sparkling wine is the sort of bottle a tourist brings home as a gift.

clue.text: Dish that is served with prune

parts.note: to prune a plant is to cut it back
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this dish is served with prunes on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' and 'prune' both pretend to be food; dish is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an attractive person is a dish, and an endearing, good-looking one is likewise called sweet or pretty.

clue.text: Trees burning in Hampshire town

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
something burning is hot

explanation.surface: Trees are ablaze in a town in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; the town is the home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The named place is a garrison town in the English county of Hampshire, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Plant concealed by wild rose rarely

indicators.note: the letters sit tucked away across the words that follow, held inside them

explanation.surface: A plant is hidden among wild roses, which seldom happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundew is the common name of this genus of insect-eating bog plant.

clue.text: Article making big noise?

definitions.meaning: a written account in a newspaper, such as a news piece
a loud bang, like the crack of a gunshot

explanation.surface: A story asks what makes a piece of writing a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a news account; the other is the sharp crack of an explosion or gunfire.

clue.text: Going back through Dudley Zoo, was in a daze

indicators.note: the run of letters is read from right to left
the letters run across the following words, inside them

explanation.surface: Someone wandered round Dudley Zoo, dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' picks YZOOW out of Dudley Zoo, was, and 'Going back' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dizzy and muddled is to be dazed, so the adjective matches the phrase.

clue.text: Very thin leek, last to be cooked

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very thin leek is the last vegetable to go in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extremely thin looks like a skeleton, all bones and no flesh.

clue.text: Man and woman saved by an adviser to desperate people

parts.note: Sam is a man's name

indicators.note: the woman is kept safe inside the word an

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man and woman rescued by a crisis counsellor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans is a British charity running a helpline for people in emotional distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Volunteers of a well-known British helpline charity counsel those in despair or contemplating suicide.

clue.text: Alien dogs barking nearby

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Alien dogs are barking somewhere close.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beside something means close at hand, so it is a synonym for adjacent.

clue.text: Feeling I missed judge's verdict

indicators.note: the letter is left out, as if missed from the word

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling was felt to have missed the point.
explanation.definitionFit: After conviction the judge pronounces the punishment, a term for the court's decision.

clue.text: Spa hotel's meal provided without a honeyed drink

parts.note: a hydro is a hotel offering spa treatments

indicators.note: the a is to be left out of the meal

explanation.surface: A spa hotel serves a meal, provided it comes without a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A out of MEAL, leaving MEL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for mead, a fermented drink made from honey and water.

clue.text: Suspended casts of EastEnders during broadcast

indicators.note: spoken in the accent of the soap's cast, where a th sound becomes f, so this is how the word sounds

parts.note: to cast something is to throw it

explanation.surface: Suspensions hit the cast of EastEnders mid-broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End; a Cockney accent says th as f, so THROWS comes out as FROZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts or payments that are suspended are said to have been frozen, a synonym.

clue.text: One embracing Lenten ritual with greater alacrity

definitions.meaning: a person who goes without food in Lent
more quickly, the comparative of quick

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person abstaining from food; the other is the comparative adverb meaning more rapidly.

clue.text: Paperwork collected by head mindlessly

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up within the following words

explanation.surface: A head teacher gathers the forms without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for administration, the routine office tasks and forms of running something.

clue.text: The perfect male Republicans in power

indicators.note: the Republicans sit inside the word for power

parts.note: might is strength or power
R is the abbreviation for Republican, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Some think the ideal man is a Republican in office.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the ideal husband or partner a person hopes to meet.

clue.text: Political philosopher shows how to spoil vote

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A political thinker demonstrates how to spoil a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl, author of Das Kapital, is a famous nineteenth-century economic and political thinker.

clue.text: Spielberg film has a lot to say

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the shark movie title; the other is a slang verb for talking incessantly.

clue.text: Revise to secure double degree in university?

indicators.note: the word for revise holds the doubled degree inside it

parts.note: to revise is to alter

indicators.note: the degree is given twice over

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Revising for a second degree at university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, meaning nourishing mother, is used for the school or college a person attended; the question mark flags that it need not be a university.

clue.text: A Welsh woman from further away?

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman wonders if she comes from somewhere more distant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Far East: someone from that continent comes from further away, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Far East comes from the far side of the world, hence a playful sense of distance.

clue.text: Repeatedly act as nark and you'll get prison

indicators.note: the action is done twice over, so the piece is written twice

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to police, as a nark does

explanation.surface: Keep informing on your mates and you'll end up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notorious jail in New York State bears this name, an example of a penitentiary.

clue.text: Satellite: vainly hope to live on it

indicators.note: the next piece is placed after the jumbled one, following on
hope that comes to nothing goes awry, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A dream of settling on a moon, which is a forlorn hope.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the moons of Saturn, an example of a natural satellite.
